findings.finding: Actual public favicon and all four PWA PNG icons are byte-identical to current old web source assets, and different from the new Desktop icon.
Desktop release workflow does not deploy Pages. Pages production publishes only main pushes; workflow_dispatch builds but skips Deploy.

Public gh-pages HEAD d43389077593abe93f8200db2dd22c7f86afb868 is the 2026-08-04 build of source cc8d04812e44ce4746f6855b88db201b6a7baba3. main subsequent HEAD f590c24de8f75c90a2a143e3c1fd32dcb73c0d8a was docs-only and did not redeploy.
HTML selects /favicon.ico and /icons/icon-256.png; manifest selects existing unversioned PWA PNGs; generated SW precaches the old bytes.

User browser favicon database, installed PWA icon, and SW cache were not inspected. They may retain old bytes after a future deployment, but cache is not the root cause because a fresh unauthenticated HTTP request already returns old bytes.

recommended_scope.source: Keep Desktop source icon pack canonical and untouched. Sync web favicon at both assets/logo/favicon.ico and rhwp-studio/public/favicon.ico, because deploy-pages.yml copies the former over the latter. Sync four web PWA PNG sizes plus Apple touch 256 from new pack. Avoid changing global logo-*.png or extension icons without separately authorized scope.
recommended_scope.cache: Use a content/version-specific favicon filename or query in index.html; update includeAssets/workbox and PWA icon URLs consistently so the installed service worker precaches the new exact resources. Distinct filename is strongest for browsers with persistent favicon URL cache.
recommended_scope.deployment: Web production is a separate main/Pages deployment, not a Desktop tag. A devel-only merge or current workflow_dispatch does not update hanpage.paldyn.com.
